newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile economy grows 7.1 pct in 1996-central bank.
newsitem.headline: Chile economy grows 7.1 pct in 1996-central bank.

text.p: Chile's economy grew 7.1 percent last year, slightly higher than the official target of seven percent, said the central bank in its fortnightly report.
"This is at the upper limit of the growth forecast made by the economic authorities for the year," said the report.
The official Imacec index showed the economy grew a surprisingly strong 8.1 percent in December compared with the same month in 1995.
Analysts had been expecting the Imacec index to show growth of between 6.8 and 7.5 percent in December.

December's growth was the result of one-off factors including a higher number of days worked and a rise in copper mining output and earlier-than-usual fruit harvests due to this year's drought, said the report.
